There are a couple of things I have to say about this. First and foremost, as an EMT, in service, we have a Duty to Act. Failure to honor that can lead to litigation and liability. If for example, I'm transporting a patient and see a MVA, I'm required by law to stop and render aid until I'm relieved by local emergency services.

Second, and this could be the loophole that the Service is using, except for extreme circumstances (mass casualty, natural disaster, etc) we cannot leave a patient in the care of a person of lower rank than us. That is considered abandonment of the patient. It could very well be that it was a paramedic that went in to aid the girl, leaving the patient with a basic or intermediate. That is a significant liability issue if the patient being transported had treatments in place that a basic or intermediate isn't qualified to deal with...being intubated, having a central line or being transported while on a narcotic drip for example.

At the end of the day, we each have to lay down and go to sleep. If this EMT has a clear conscious about his choice, then I support him. Given what I know about this case, I believe I would act similarly.

CICO still applies whether you get your daily calories from fresh, whole foods, or 100% of your calories are coming from M&Ms. If you are eating a deficit of either of those things, you will still lose weight. However, with the M&Ms, you will be extremely hungry (1200 calories of M&Ms is only about 1.5 cups) and you will be extremely deficient in many nutrients if you continue to eat only M&Ms long-term.

A fairer statement would be "not all calories are created equal" because some calories (like those in whole foods) also contain vitamins and nutrients. Calories in junk food do not contain vitamins and nutrients, and this is why they are often referred to as "empty calories."
